[element-index-entry]
=== `<index-entry>` Index Entry

One entry, with all its subdivisions, see and see also terms, and navigational pointers (if any) presented in a structural index.

#### Attributes

* <<attribute-content-type,`@content-type`>>
* <<attribute-sort-key,`@sort-key`>>
* <<attribute-specific-use,`@specific-use`>>
#### Base Attributes

* <<attribute-id,`@id`>>
* <<attribute-xml-base,`@xml:base`>>
* <<attribute-xml-lang,`@xml:lang`>>

#### Models and Context

#### May be contained in

<<element-index,`<index>`>>, <<element-index-div,`<index-div>`>>, <<element-index-entry,`<index-entry>`>>
#### Description

The following, in order: <<element-term,`<term>`>> <<element-term,Term>> Any combination of: <<element-index-entry,`<index-entry>`>> <<element-index-entry,Index Entry>> <<element-ext-link,`<ext-link>`>> <<element-ext-link,External Link>> <<element-nav-pointer,`<nav-pointer>`>> <<element-nav-pointer,Navigation Pointer>> <<element-nav-pointer-group,`<nav-pointer-group>`>> <<element-nav-pointer-group,Navigation Pointer Group>> <<element-see-entry,`<see-entry>`>> <<element-see-entry,See Structural Index Entry>> <<element-see-also-entry,`<see-also-entry>`>> <<element-see-also-entry,See-Also Structural Index Entry>>
#### Content Model

[source,xml]
....
<!ELEMENT  index-entry  %index-entry-model;                          >
....
#### Expanded Content Model

(term, (index-entry | ext-link | nav-pointer | nav-pointer-group | see-entry | see-also-entry)*)

#### Tagged Samples

#### In index, with page numbers

[source,xml]
....
...
<back>
 <index>
  <index-title-group>
   <title>INDEX</title>
  </index-title-group>
  <index-entry>
   <term>Abbreviations</term>
   <nav-pointer-group
    ><nav-pointer specific-use="paragraph" rid="idx869"/>
    <nav-pointer specific-use="page">7</nav-pointer></nav-pointer-group>
  </index-entry>

  <index-entry>
   <term>Acquisition Management Systems Control (AMSC) number</term>
   <nav-pointer-group
    ><nav-pointer specific-use="paragraph" rid="idx284"/>
    <nav-pointer specific-use="page">2</nav-pointer></nav-pointer-group>
   <nav-pointer-group
    ><nav-pointer specific-use="paragraph" rid="idx752"/>
    <nav-pointer specific-use="page">6</nav-pointer></nav-pointer-group>
   <nav-pointer-group
    ><nav-pointer specific-use="paragraph" rid="idx1235"/>
    <nav-pointer specific-use="page">19</nav-pointer></nav-pointer-group>
  </index-entry>
 </index>
 ...
</back>
...

#### In index with alphabetical divisions

[source,xml]
....
...
<back>
 <index>
  <index-title-group>
   <title>INDEX</title>
  </index-title-group>
  ...

  <index-div>
   <index-title-group>
    <title>D</title>
   </index-title-group>
   <index-entry>
    <term>degree of linear polarization</term>
    <nav-pointer-group
     ><nav-pointer specific-use="section" rid="sec_3.41"/></nav-pointer-group>
   </index-entry>

   <index-entry>
    <term>device efficiency</term>
    <nav-pointer-group
     ><nav-pointer specific-use="section" rid="sec_3.18"/></nav-pointer-group>
   </index-entry>

   <index-entry>
    <term>divergence angle</term>
    <nav-pointer-group
     ><nav-pointer specific-use="section" rid="sec_3.19.1"/>, 
     <nav-pointer specific-use="section" rid="sec_3.19.2"/></nav-pointer-group>
   </index-entry>
  </index-div>
  ...

 </index>
 ...
</back>

#### Another index with alphabetical divisions, where entry includes page range

[source,xml]
....
...
<back>
 <index>
  <index-title-group><title>Index</title></index-title-group>
  <index-div>
   <index-title-group><title>A</title></index-title-group>
   ...
   <index-entry>
    <term>access vocabularies</term>
    <see-entry>entry terms</see-entry>
   </index-entry>
   ...
   <index-entry>
    <term>adjectives</term>
    <nav-pointer-group
     ><nav-pointer rid="idx320" nav-pointer-type="start-of-range"
     >26</nav-pointer>&ndash;<nav-pointer rid="idx486" nav-pointer-type="end-of-range"
     >27</nav-pointer></nav-pointer-group>    
    <see-also-entry>modifiers in compound terms</see-also-entry>
   </index-entry>
   ...
  </index-div>
  ...
 </index>
</back>
...
....
